raw_response:
I'm 60 this year, been farming these 12 mu in Quzhou for 35 years. Never went to school, can't read those words on the fertilizer bags. But I know this land, and I know what works.

My 8 mu of winter wheat went in last October, same as always. I used seeds I saved from two years ago — good plump kernels, no need to waste money on store-bought seed. At planting I spread one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu, about 50 kg. That was the base. Now it's April, the wheat is getting tall. I'm going to spread more fertilizer soon — about half a bag of urea per mu, I do this every year when the wheat starts growing fast. If it doesn't rain I'll water two more times before harvest in June. My neighbor Old Li put less fertilizer last year and his wheat turned yellow before heading — I'm not making that mistake. Better to spend a bit more than risk losing half the crop. For weeds I already sprayed once after planting, and if I see aphids I'll spray insecticide once. I should get about 750 jin per mu, same as usual.

The cotton is going in this week on my 4 mu plot. I bought new cotton seed this year because my saved seed didn't sprout well last time. I put down almost one bag of compound fertilizer per mu in the furrows at planting — about 40 kg. Cotton gets hungry later, so I'll add urea once when it flowers, about 15 kg. Water costs money — the electric pump isn't cheap — so I'll irrigate twice, at flowering and when the bolls form. Cotton always has bollworms, so I spray insecticide three times and herbicide once. The poison costs a lot but without it the worms eat everything. Picking is hard work — my wife and I will do most of it, but I might hire a few days of help. If the weather is good I can get maybe 500 jin per mu.

For maize, I plant right after wheat harvest in June — the window is tight, maybe five days. I'll hire my nephew's tractor to plow, or rent one from the village. I buy hybrid maize seed, 2 kg per mu. I put compound fertilizer in the planting holes, about 40 kg per mu, and add urea once when the maize is knee-high, about 18 kg. Maize doesn't need as much water — I'll irrigate twice if it's dry. One spray for weeds at planting, and maybe insecticide if the armyworms come. I expect about 800 jin per mu.

Money is tight. I'm spending close to 6,000 yuan on all these inputs this year. My son works in a factory in the city and sends some money home, but I don't like relying on that. My wife and I do most of the farm work ourselves. Cotton takes the most labor with all the hoeing, pruning, and picking, but it brings in the cash we need. I'm doing what I've always done — it works well enough, and changing things is risky when you don't have much money.
